title: Messaging Reliability, Idempotency, and Retries
description: Learn how to make your messaging systems reliable using idempotency, retries, and dead-letter patterns.

data.text: In distributed systems, networks fail, services restart, and messages can be delivered more than once. Reliable messaging means your application handles these situations gracefully without duplicating work or losing data.

terms.definition: Processing the same message multiple times produces the same result as processing it once.
Azure guarantees messages are delivered at least once, but possibly more than once.
A guarantee that each message is processed exactly one time. Azure Service Bus Premium tier offers this for queues.
When many clients retry failed operations simultaneously, overwhelming the server.

data.text: The best way to handle duplicate messages is to make your handlers idempotent. Store the message ID in a database and check if it has already been processed before performing the action.

data.title: Common Retry Patterns
items: Fixed Interval: Retry after a constant delay (for example, 5 seconds).
Exponential Backoff: Double the delay after each failure (1s, 2s, 4s, 8s...).
Exponential Backoff with Jitter: Add randomness to prevent synchronized retries across clients.
Circuit Breaker: Stop retrying after too many failures and wait before trying again.

data.title: Idempotency Is Key
data.text: No retry strategy is perfect. Combine retries with idempotent operations so that even if a message is processed twice, your data stays consistent.
